post:
Since 1 January 2026, neighbours in Switzerland can share their rooftop solar in a local electricity community. Someone then has to send every member a bill each month, from 15-minute meter data that has gaps, duplicates and two daylight-saving days a year.

I built an open-source tool for that billing step. It reads 15-minute readings per member and per PV plant, cleans them, allocates the solar energy with a proportional, static or hybrid key, applies the 40% grid-fee reduction from the ordinance and ElCom 2026 tariffs, and writes one CSV line and a one-page German PDF statement per member and month, plus producer credit notes and a community summary.

Measured on a simulated community of 12 households and 2 PV plants for a full year:
- 0 Wh allocation error in 35,040 quarter-hours, and members' payments match producer credits to the Rappen.
- The allocation key changed a household's yearly bill by at most CHF 5.79.
- 200 members billed for a year in 190 s, including 2,412 PDFs.

Not verified: the meter data is simulated, there is no real utility data exchange yet, and it is not legal or tax advice.

If you run a community: would you pick the allocation key members understand, or the one the grid operator uses?

Code: https://github.com/Usernamepersonperson/leg-member-statements
